summary: A responsive school website with a three-image hero slider, an online application and status-check workflow, school history, leadership profiles, published announcements, and a PHP/MySQL staff portal for applications, student records, and academic data.

services.name: School Website
services.description: Responsive HTML, CSS, and JavaScript school website with a three-image hero slider, study options, public applications and status checks, school history, leadership profiles, and announcements.

services.name: School Management Backend
services.description: PHP 8 public application and status endpoints plus staff portal and MySQL database for staff authentication, application review, student records, departments, programmes, courses, academic sessions, and announcements.

questions.question: What is the school's official name, which officials should be featured (names and titles), and what school-history text should appear? Please also identify or provide the photos for the officials and the three hero backgrounds (or say that suitable placeholders should be used for now).
questions.answer: School name: FEDERAL POLYTECHNIC KAMPE, ILLIONIS. Display location: Illinois, Kwara State. Founded in 1980 by Prof. Praise Stephen (Vice Chancellor); the school welcomes students to learn different courses and develop skills. Officials: Prof. Praise Stephen (Vice Chancellor), Dr. Engr. Salihu Daabu (Deputy Vice Chancellor), Dr. Shuaibu (Registrar), and Hon. Nasiru A (Bursar). Use replaceable photo placeholders for officials. Use the supplied front-gate photo for hero slide 1 and school-compound photo for slide 2; keep the local illustration for slide 3 until another photo is supplied.

questions.question: Should admissions remain information-only, or include applicant submissions and staff review?
questions.answer: Add a public application form and a staff application-review workflow. Applicants receive a reference code and can check status using the code and their email address.

questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing for a maintainable frontend.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses standard JavaScript without a separate type system.

questions.rationale: The small static site uses plain JavaScript for the slideshow and mobile navigation.

questions.question: Which frontend framework or approach do you prefer?

options.label: React
options.description: Component-based framework with a broad ecosystem.

options.label: Vue
options.description: Progressive framework with approachable component development.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: Compiler-based framework for compact interactive experiences.

options.label: Angular
options.description: Full-featured framework with an integrated application architecture.

options.label: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript
options.description: A minimal approach for a small brochure-style website.

questions.rationale: A lightweight static site avoids unnecessary framework and build dependencies.

questions.question: Which data stores are needed for staff accounts, student records, academic structure, and school announcements?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only content and assets bundled with the website; cannot be combined with another store.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Store and serve the hero background images and officials' photos.

options.label: MySQL
options.description: Store staff accounts, applicant submissions, student records, departments, programmes, courses, sessions, and announcements.

questions.rationale: The backend uses MySQL for staff authentication, applicant submissions, student records, academic structure, and announcements; image assets remain local files.

questions.question: Will users sign in to access application features?

options.label: No
options.description: The website is public and has no sign-in-gated application features.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in to access application features.

questions.rationale: School staff sign in to manage private student information and public announcements; the public website remains available without sign-in.
